name: How do I make the exposed end of a kitchen peninsula look finished?

mainEntity.name: How do I make the exposed end of a kitchen peninsula look finished?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A finished end panel, decorative side, or matching cabinet treatment is needed if the peninsula end is visible from the room. Leaving a cabinet side unfinished can make the installation look incomplete and may not protect the cabinet material adequately.

Context: The visible end often faces the dining or living area, so it should be included in the design rather than treated as an afterthought. The treatment may also need to coordinate with the countertop edge and toe kick.

Key factors:
- Which sides are visible
- Cabinet finish and material availability
- Countertop edge profile
- Seating or support hardware

Practical guidance: Mark visible faces on the elevation and include them in the written proposal. Confirm how seams, fillers, end panels, and toe kicks will be finished.

Elite Remodeling & Design can incorporate finish selections into a coordinated kitchen design.
acceptedAnswer.description: Specify a finished end panel, decorative side, or matching cabinet treatment for every visible surface. Coordinate it with the countertop edge, toe kick, fillers, and seating support, and ensure the proposal lists those finish details explicitly.
